pages.title: Making days
pages.content: Every day in the shop follows the same hours: Tomás roasts at 08:00, Noor tempers on the marble slab at 10:00, Lukas fills the moulds at 12:00 and Adaeze glazes the cakes at 15:00.

pages.title: Tasting
pages.content: Tasting flights at the counter are EUR 9.00; seated tastings run Thursday to Sunday at 11:00, 14:00 and 16:00 for EUR 22.00 per person.

pages.title: Cake orders
pages.content: Dark ganache 70%, Hazelnut praline and Cocoa and pear, in 18 cm (EUR 42.00) or 22 cm (EUR 58.00). Order three days ahead; collect Friday to Sunday, 11:00–17:00.

pages.title: Bars & bonbons
pages.content: Single-origin bars (70 g, EUR 7.50) and bonbon boxes of nine (EUR 18.00), made in the shop from five seasonal origins.

pages.title: Prices
pages.content: Prices in EUR including VAT. Cakes are paid at collection.

pages.title: About
pages.content: Kaoru Cocoa was founded in 2017 by Noor Halvorsen at 14 Linden Arcade, Harrowfield.

pages.title: Visit
pages.content: 14 Linden Arcade, Harrowfield. Open Tuesday to Sunday, 09:00–18:00; closed on Mondays.

pages.title: Newsletter

posts.title: Why we temper at ten
posts.excerpt: Noor on the tempering curve, the morning slab, and why a batch made at ten is best the same afternoon.
posts.content:
Noor Halvorsen starts tempering at ten because the shop is quiet, the slab is cool from the night and the beans Tomás roasted at eight have rested just long enough. Melted chocolate is spread and gathered on the marble until it cools to the working temperature, then warmed a few degrees so only the stable crystals remain.

That small curve is what gives a bar its snap and its shine. A batch tempered well keeps its gloss for weeks, but it tastes brightest within days of tabling, which is why we plan the counter around the morning slab and serve the same afternoon.

Come in at ten and watch through the glass screen, four metres from the counter. The scent is the reason the shop has its name.

posts.title: Building a tasting flight
posts.excerpt: Priya on choosing three squares and a small cocoa from the day's batch.
posts.content:
A tasting flight at the counter is three 10 g squares from today's batch and a small cocoa, EUR 9.00. Priya Raman picks the squares so each one differs from the last: first the brightest, then the roundest, then the darkest.

She suggests tasting in that order, letting each square melt slowly on the tongue before the next. The small cocoa comes last, made from the same origin as the middle square so the two can be compared.

For a longer hour, the seated tasting on Thursday to Sunday adds six bars across the five origins, two bonbons and a cocoa, forty-five minutes for up to six guests.
